texts.text: Glossary of Grinding Terms

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Arc of Cut: The part of the wheel that contacts the workpiece.
texts.text: Arc of Cut: The part of the wheel that contacts the workpiece.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Aspect Ratio: The ratio of an abrasive's length to its width. grain

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Cermet: A heat-resistant alloy formed by compacting and sintering together a metal and a ceramic material.
texts.text: Cermet: A heat-resistant alloy formed by compacting and sintering together a metal and a ceramic material.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Continuous Dressing: A process where a diamond dressing roll sharpens the grinding wheel by removing dull grits all the time the wheel is machining the workpiece.
texts.text: Continuous Dressing: A process where a diamond dressing roll sharpens the grinding wheel by removing dull grits all the time the wheel is machining the workpiece.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Creep-Feed Grinding: A process where a very soft and porous grinding wheel takes a deep cut in one slow pass. Well-suited for difficult-to-machine materials, the process offer a high stock-removal rate

texts.orig: Cylindrical Grinding: A process for machining round components.
texts.text: Cylindrical Grinding: A process for machining round components.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Dressing: Removal of undesirable material from a "loaded" grinding wheel by using a diamond tool
texts.text: Dressing: Removal of undesirable material from a "loaded" grinding wheel by using a diamond tool

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Friability: The ability of an abrasive to fracture.
texts.text: Friability: The ability of an abrasive to fracture.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Hard Turning: Turning hardened metal on a lathe to eliminate grinding it.
texts.text: Hard Turning: Turning hardened metal on a lathe to eliminate grinding it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: ID Grinding: A process that removes metal from the inside diameter of holes or profiles by applying a very small, high-rpm grinding wheel.
texts.text: ID Grinding: A process that removes metal from the inside diameter of holes or profiles by applying a very small, high-rpm grinding wheel.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Reciprocal Grinding: A process where the workpiece is mounted on a table that moves back and forth beneath the grinding wheel.
texts.text: Reciprocal Grinding: A process where the workpiece is mounted on a table that moves back and forth beneath the grinding wheel.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Swarf: The mass of chips and debris remaining after grinding.
texts.text: Swarf: The mass of chips and debris remaining after grinding.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Truing: Application of a diamond tool to a grinding wheel to ensure roundness and concentricity.
texts.text: Truing: Application of a diamond tool to a grinding wheel to ensure roundness and concentricity.

texts.orig: Care must be taken to apply the grinding fluid properly to plated and metal bond grinding wheels to prevent them from hydroplaning. Significant hydrodynamic pressures in the arc of cut can lift the wheel from the workpiece surface; resulting in poor surface finish and high wheel wear.
